Tu mapa en `portfolio-grid.tsx` es un mapa estático centrado en (40.275, -3.915) con un marcador rojo, dentro de una tarjeta de portfolio. Estos plugins encajan bien con ese uso:

## Recomendados para tu caso

### 1. **maplibre-preload**
- Precarga tiles para que el pan/zoom sea más fluido.
- Configuración mínima.
- Útil si el usuario interactúa con el mapa.

### 2. **map-gl-style-switcher** o **maplibre-gl-basemaps**
- Permiten cambiar entre estilos (claro/oscuro/satélite).
- Útil si quieres que el mapa siga el tema del portfolio o dar más opciones al usuario.
- `map-gl-style-switcher` tiene wrapper para `react-map-gl`.

### 3. **mapbox-gl-infobox**
- Muestra un popup/infobox al hacer clic en el marcador.
- Ideal para mostrar algo como “Madrid, España” o una breve descripción de tu ubicación.

### 4. **geojson-map-fit-mercator**
- Calcula el mejor centro, zoom y bearing para encuadrar varios puntos.
- Útil si más adelante añades varios proyectos con ubicación y quieres encuadrarlos todos automáticamente.

### 5. **mapbox-gl-language** o **Diplomat**
- Localizan etiquetas del mapa al idioma del usuario.
- Tiene sentido si el portfolio es multilingüe.

---

## Opcionales

- **maplibre-transition**: transiciones suaves al cambiar de estilo (si usas style switcher).
- **maplibre-glass-css**: tema tipo glass para los controles del mapa.
- **maplibre-gl-export**: si quieres permitir exportar el mapa como imagen.

---

## No recomendados para tu caso

- Geocoding, routing, dibujo/edición, medidas, terreno, animaciones temporales, comparación de mapas, 3D, etc. Son demasiado para un mapa de ubicación en un portfolio.

Si quieres, puedo ayudarte a integrar uno concreto (por ejemplo `maplibre-preload` o `map-gl-style-switcher`) en tu componente.

README\n\n# Map GL Style Switcher\n\nA TypeScript control for switching Mapbox GL / MapLibre GL map styles. Easily add a floating style switcher to your map app, with support for multiple styles, images, dark/light themes, and before/after change callbacks.\n\nAvailable as:\n\n- &#96;StyleSwitcherControl&#96; - Direct IControl implementation for Mapbox/MapLibre GL\n\n- &#96;MapGLStyleSwitcher&#96; - React component for react-map-gl integration\n\n- &#96;useStyleSwitcher&#96; - React hook for custom map instances\n\n[🌐 Live Demo](https://map-gl-style-switcher.netlify.app/)\n\n## Animated Demo\n\n## Available Styles\n\n## Features\n\n- IControl implementation for Mapbox GL / MapLibre GL\n\n- React component for react-map-gl integration\n\n- React hook for custom map instances\n\n- Floating style switcher in any corner (via map.addControl position)\n\n- Support for multiple map styles with thumbnails\n\n- Expand/collapse on hover with smooth animations\n\n- Dark/light/auto theme support — &#96;theme: 'auto'&#96; reacts to OS preference changes in real time\n\n- RTL text support for Arabic/Hebrew interfaces\n\n- Configurable display options (show/hide labels and images)\n\n- Callbacks for before/after style change\n\n- &#96;updateOptions()&#96; for imperative option updates after mount\n\n- Fully customizable CSS classes\n\n- TypeScript support\n\n- Accessibility features (ARIA labels, keyboard navigation)\n\n- ESM-only package (tree-shakeable, no CommonJS bundle)\n\n- Comprehensive test coverage\n\n## Install\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\n# Using npm (recommended)\nnpm install map-gl-style-switcher\n\n# Using yarn\nyarn add map-gl-style-switcher\n\n# Using pnpm\npnpm add map-gl-style-switcher\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&gt; Note: This package ships ES modules only. CommonJS &#96;require()&#96; is not supported. All modern bundlers (Vite, webpack 5, Rollup, esbuild) handle ESM natively.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Vanilla JS / Direct MapLibre or Mapbox GL\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { StyleSwitcherControl, type StyleItem } from 'map-gl-style-switcher';\nimport 'map-gl-style-switcher/dist/map-gl-style-switcher.css';\n\nconst styles: StyleItem[] = [\n{\nid: 'voyager',\nname: 'Voyager',\nimage:\n'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muimsd/map-gl-style-switcher/refs/heads/main/public/voyager.png',\nstyleUrl: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/voyager-gl-style/style.json',\ndescription: 'Voyager style from Carto',\n},\n{\nid: 'positron',\nname: 'Positron',\nimage:\n'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muimsd/map-gl-style-switcher/refs/heads/main/public/positron.png',\nstyleUrl: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json',\ndescription: 'Positron style from Carto',\n},\n];\n\nconst control = new StyleSwitcherControl({\nstyles,\nactiveStyleId: 'voyager',\ntheme: 'auto',\nonAfterStyleChange: (_from, to) =&gt; {\nmap.setStyle(to.styleUrl);\n},\n});\n\nmap.addControl(control, 'bottom-left');\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### React — useStyleSwitcher hook (custom map instance)\n\nUse this when you manage the map instance yourself (e.g., inside &#96;useEffect&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';\nimport maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';\nimport { useStyleSwitcher, type StyleItem } from 'map-gl-style-switcher/react';\nimport 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';\nimport 'map-gl-style-switcher/dist/map-gl-style-switcher.css';\n\nconst styles: StyleItem[] = [\n/* ... */\n];\n\nfunction MapComponent() {\nconst mapContainer = useRef(null);\nconst mapRef = useRef(null);\n\nuseEffect(() =&gt; {\nif (!mapContainer.current) return;\nmapRef.current = new maplibregl.Map({\ncontainer: mapContainer.current,\nstyle: styles[0].styleUrl,\ncenter: [0, 0],\nzoom: 2,\n});\nreturn () =&gt; mapRef.current?.remove();\n}, []);\n\nuseStyleSwitcher(mapRef.current, {\nstyles,\ntheme: 'auto',\nposition: 'bottom-left',\nonAfterStyleChange: (_from, to) =&gt; {\nmapRef.current?.setStyle(to.styleUrl);\n},\n});\n\nreturn ;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&gt; Tip: The hook recreates the control whenever options change (deep comparison via JSON serialisation). Pass stable object references or memoize options if performance is critical.\n\n### React — MapGLStyleSwitcher component (react-map-gl)\n\nUse this when your map is rendered by &#96;react-map-gl&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Map } from 'react-map-gl/maplibre';\nimport { MapGLStyleSwitcher, type StyleItem } from 'map-gl-style-switcher/react-map-gl';\nimport 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';\nimport 'map-gl-style-switcher/dist/map-gl-style-switcher.css';\n\nconst styles: StyleItem[] = [\n/* ... */\n];\n\nfunction MyMap() {\nconst [mapStyle, setMapStyle] = useState(styles[0].styleUrl);\nconst [activeStyleId, setActiveStyleId] = useState(styles[0].id);\n\nconst handleStyleChange = (styleUrl: string) =&gt; {\nsetMapStyle(styleUrl);\nconst style = styles.find(s =&gt; s.styleUrl === styleUrl);\nif (style) setActiveStyleId(style.id);\n};\n\nreturn (\n\n);\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;MapGLStyleSwitcher&#96; propagates all non-callback prop changes to the underlying control after mount — changing &#96;activeStyleId&#96;, &#96;theme&#96;, &#96;showLabels&#96;, &#96;styles&#96;, etc. is fully reactive. Callbacks (&#96;onBeforeStyleChange&#96;, &#96;onAfterStyleChange&#96;, &#96;onStyleChange&#96;) are always up-to-date via refs and do not cause the control to be recreated.\n\n## Examples\n\n### MapLibre GL Example\n\n[View the maplibre example →](/muimsd/map-gl-style-switcher/blob/main/examples/maplibre)\n\n### React Map GL Example\n\n[View the react-map-gl example →](/muimsd/map-gl-style-switcher/blob/main/examples/react-map-gl)\n\n## Configuration Options\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface StyleSwitcherControlOptions {\nstyles: StyleItem[]; // Array of map styles (required)\nactiveStyleId?: string; // Active style ID (default: first style)\nonBeforeStyleChange?: (from: StyleItem, to: StyleItem) =&gt; void; // Called before style changes\nonAfterStyleChange?: (from: StyleItem, to: StyleItem) =&gt; void; // Called after style changes\nshowLabels?: boolean; // Show style names (default: true)\nshowImages?: boolean; // Show thumbnails (default: true)\nanimationDuration?: number; // Expand animation in ms (default: 200)\nmaxHeight?: number; // Max list height in px (default: 300)\ntheme?: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'; // UI theme (default: 'light')\nclassNames?: Partial; // Custom CSS class overrides\nrtl?: boolean; // RTL layout (default: false)\n}\n\ninterface StyleItem {\nid: string; // Unique identifier\nname: string; // Display name\nimage: string; // Thumbnail URL or data URI\nstyleUrl: string; // MapLibre/Mapbox style URL\ndescription?: string; // Optional tooltip text\n}\n\ninterface StyleSwitcherClassNames {\ncontainer: string; // Main container class\nlist: string; // Expanded list container class\nitem: string; // Individual style item class\nitemSelected: string; // Selected item class\nitemHideLabel: string; // No-label utility class\ndark: string; // Dark theme class\nlight: string; // Light theme class\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Option details\n\n- &#96;activeStyleId&#96;: Controls both the initially selected style and what is shown in the collapsed state. When using &#96;MapGLStyleSwitcher&#96;, updating this prop reactively switches the highlighted style.\n\n- &#96;showLabels&#96; &amp; &#96;showImages&#96;: At least one must be &#96;true&#96; (throws otherwise).\n\n- &#96;theme&#96;:\n\n&#96;'light'&#96;: Light colour scheme (default)\n&#96;'dark'&#96;: Dark colour scheme\n&#96;'auto'&#96;: Follows the OS preference and updates automatically when the user switches between light and dark mode\n\n- &#96;rtl&#96;: Enables right-to-left layout for Arabic/Hebrew interfaces.\n\n### Imperative updates — updateOptions()\n\nAfter adding the control to a map you can update its options without recreating it:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nconst control = new StyleSwitcherControl({ styles, activeStyleId: 'voyager' });\nmap.addControl(control, 'bottom-left');\n\n// Later — switch active style programmatically\ncontrol.updateOptions({ activeStyleId: 'positron' });\n\n// Or change multiple options at once\ncontrol.updateOptions({ theme: 'dark', showLabels: false });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOnly the keys you pass are updated; all others remain unchanged. If the control has already been added to the map, the UI re-renders immediately.\n\n## Customizing CSS Classes\n\nOverride all CSS classes used by the control via the &#96;classNames&#96; option:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nconst control = new StyleSwitcherControl({\nstyles,\nclassNames: {\ncontainer: 'my-style-switcher',\nlist: 'my-style-list',\nitem: 'my-style-item',\nitemSelected: 'my-style-item-selected',\nitemHideLabel: 'my-style-item-hide-label',\ndark: 'my-style-dark',\nlight: 'my-style-light',\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Contributing\n\nWe welcome contributions! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request. [vitest.config.ts](https://github.com/popkinj/maplibre-transition/blob/main/vitest.config.ts)\n\n## README\n\n# Maplibre Transition Plugin\n\nA utility plugin for Maplibre GL JS that adds feature level transition-related functionality.\n\n## Compatibility\n\nThis plugin is compatible with MapLibre GL JS version 3.0.0 and above.\n\n## Installation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnpm install maplibre-transition\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Usage\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport maplibregl from \"maplibre-gl\";\nimport MaplibreTransition from \"maplibre-transition\";\n\nconst map = new maplibregl.Map({\ncontainer: \"map\",\nstyle: \"https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json\",\ncenter: [0, 0],\nzoom: 2,\n});\n\n// Initialize the plugin\nMaplibreTransition.init(map);\n\n// Use the plugin with either method\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 1000,\ndelay: 500,\nease: \"linear\",\npaint: {\n\"fill-opacity\": [0.1, 1],\n},\n});\n\n// Or use the shorthand method (deprecated)\nmap.T(feature, {\nduration: 1000,\ndelay: 500,\nease: \"linear\",\npaint: {\n\"fill-opacity\": [0.1, 1],\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&gt; Note: The &#96;map.T&#96; method is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Please use &#96;map.transition&#96; for new code.\n\n## Transitioning Multiple Properties\n\nYou can transition multiple style properties simultaneously by specifying them in the &#96;paint&#96; object:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 1000,\npaint: {\n\"circle-radius\": [8, 12],\n\"circle-stroke-width\": [2, 4],\n\"circle-opacity\": [1, 0.2],\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAll specified properties will transition together using the same duration and easing function. This is useful for creating coordinated visual effects.\n\n## Easing Types\n\nThe plugin supports the following easing functions from d3-ease:\n\n- &#96;\"linear\"&#96; - Linear interpolation (no easing)\n\n- &#96;\"quad\"&#96; - Quadratic easing (smooth acceleration/deceleration)\n\n- &#96;\"cubic\"&#96; - Cubic easing (stronger acceleration/deceleration)\n\n- &#96;\"elastic\"&#96; - Elastic easing (bouncy effect)\n\n- &#96;\"bounce\"&#96; - Bounce easing (multiple bounces)\n\n- &#96;\"circle\"&#96; - Circular easing (circular acceleration/deceleration)\n\n- &#96;\"exp\"&#96; - Exponential easing (exponential acceleration/deceleration)\n\n- &#96;\"poly\"&#96; - Polynomial easing (configurable power)\n\n- &#96;\"sin\"&#96; - Sinusoidal easing (smooth sine wave)\n\nExample with different easing:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 1000,\nease: \"elastic\", // Try different easing functions\npaint: {\n\"fill-opacity\": [0.1, 1],\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Color Transitions\n\nThe plugin supports smooth color transitions using D3's color interpolation. It automatically detects color values and uses the appropriate color space for interpolation:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 1000,\nease: \"linear\",\npaint: {\n\"fill-color\": [\"#ff0000\", \"#00ff00\"], // RGB color transition\n\"fill-outline-color\": [\"hsl(0,100%,50%)\", \"hsl(120,100%,50%)\"], // HSL color transition\n\"fill-opacity\": [0.1, 1],\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe plugin supports the following color formats:\n\n- RGB colors (e.g., \"#ff0000\", \"rgb(255,0,0)\")\n\n- HSL colors (e.g., \"hsl(0,100%,50%)\")\n\n- LAB colors (e.g., \"lab(50,100,0)\")\n\nEach color format uses its appropriate interpolation method:\n\n- RGB interpolation for RGB colors\n\n- HSL interpolation for HSL colors (better for hue transitions)\n\n- LAB interpolation for LAB colors (perceptually uniform)\n\n## Chaining Transitions\n\nYou can chain transitions using the &#96;onComplete&#96; callback. This is useful for creating complex animations that need to happen in sequence:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 600,\nease: \"elastic\",\npaint: {\n\"circle-radius\": [8, 12],\n\"circle-color\": [\"#ff0000\", \"#00ff00\"], // Color transition\n},\nonComplete: () =&gt; {\n// This transition will start after the radius transition completes\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 300,\nease: \"linear\",\npaint: {\n\"circle-stroke-width\": [2, 4],\n\"circle-opacity\": [1, 0.2],\n\"circle-color\": [\"#00ff00\", \"#0000ff\"], // Another color transition\n},\n});\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can combine multiple properties in both the initial and chained transitions. This allows for complex animations where some properties change together, while others follow in sequence.\n\n## Advanced Transitions with Multiple Breakpoints\n\nThe plugin supports multiple breakpoints in transition arrays, enabling complex animations and color cycles. This feature allows for smooth transitions between multiple states or creating color cycling effects.\n\n### Color Transitions with Multiple Breakpoints\n\nYou can specify multiple colors to create smooth color cycles:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 3000,\nease: \"elastic\",\npaint: {\n\"fill-color\": [\n\"#088\", // Start with green\n\"#f00\", // Then red\n\"#00f\", // Then blue\n\"#ff0\", // Then yellow\n\"#f0f\", // Then magenta\n\"#0ff\", // Then cyan\n\"#088\", // Back to green\n],\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe plugin automatically interpolates between adjacent colors, creating smooth transitions. The interpolation respects the color space (RGB, HSL, or LAB) of the input colors.\n\n### Numeric Transitions with Multiple Breakpoints\n\nMultiple breakpoints also work for numeric properties, creating piecewise linear interpolations:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 2000,\nease: \"cubic\",\npaint: {\n\"circle-radius\": [0, 10, 5, 15, 8], // Complex size animation\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis creates a smooth transition that:\n\n- Grows from 0 to 10\n\n- Shrinks to 5\n\n- Grows to 15\n\n- Finally settles at 8\n\n### Best Practices for Multiple Breakpoints\n\n- Duration: Use longer durations (2000-3000ms) when working with multiple breakpoints to make transitions more visible and smooth.\n\n- Easing Selection:\n\n&#96;elastic&#96; or &#96;bounce&#96;: Best for playful, dynamic effects\n&#96;cubic&#96; or &#96;sin&#96;: Ideal for smooth, professional transitions\n&#96;linear&#96;: Use for precise, mechanical movements\n\n- Color Space Considerations:\n\nRGB: Best for direct color transitions\nHSL: Better for hue-based transitions\nLAB: Best for perceptually uniform transitions\n\n- Performance: While multiple breakpoints are supported, consider the number of breakpoints you use. More breakpoints mean more interpolation calculations.\n\nExample combining multiple properties with breakpoints:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.transition(feature, {\nduration: 3000,\nease: \"elastic\",\npaint: {\n\"fill-color\": [\"#088\", \"#f00\", \"#00f\", \"#088\"],\n\"circle-radius\": [5, 15, 10, 20],\n\"fill-opacity\": [1, 0.5, 0.8, 1],\n},\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Live Demo\n\nInteractive demos are available at: [https://popkinj.github.io/maplibre-transition/](https://popkinj.github.io/maplibre-transition/)\n\nThe demo site includes examples for:\n\n- Basic Transition - Simple radius transitions on click\n\n- Color Animation - Color property transitions\n\n- Color Cycling - Multi-breakpoint color cycles\n\n- Easing Functions - Compare all 9 easing types\n\n- Multiple Properties - Animate several properties together\n\n- Chained Transitions - Sequential animation chains\n\n- Hover Effects - Mouse-triggered transitions\n\n- Multi-Breakpoint - Complex piecewise animations\n\n- Vector Tiles - Transitions with vector tile sources\n\n## Development\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\n# Install dependencies\nnpm install\n\n# Build the plugin\nnpm run build\n\n# Run the development environment\nnpm run dev\n\n# Open the development webserver that refreshes on saving.\nnpm run serve\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Testing\n\nThe project includes comprehensive unit and E2E tests.\n\n### Unit Tests (Vitest)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\n# Run unit tests\nnpm test\n\n# Run tests in watch mode\nnpm run test:watch\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### E2E Tests (Playwright)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\n# Run E2E tests (headless)\nnpm run test:e2e\n\n# Run E2E tests with interactive UI\nnpm run test:e2e:ui\n\n# Run E2E tests in headed browser\nnpm run test:e2e:headed\n\n# Run all tests (unit + E2E)\nnpm run test:all\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Deployment\n\n### Deploy Demo Pages to GitHub Pages\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnpm run deploy:examples\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis deploys the &#96;examples/&#96; directory to the &#96;gh-pages&#96; branch, making demos available at &#96;https://popkinj.github.io/maplibre-transition/&#96;."
}

  "markdown": "# osm-americana/diplomat\n\nInternationalization plugin for MapLibre GL JS. Contribute to osm-americana/diplomat development by creating an account on GitHub.\n\n⭐ 14 stars | 🍴 1 forks\n\n## Links\n\n- [Repository](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat)\n- [Issues](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/issues)\n- [Pull Requests](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/pulls)\n\n## Files\n\n- [.github/](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/tree/main/.github)\n- [docs/](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/tree/main/docs)\n- [example/](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/tree/main/example)\n- [test/](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/tree/main/test)\n- [.gitattributes](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/.gitattributes)\n- [.gitignore](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/.gitignore)\n- [.npmrc](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/.npmrc)\n- [.prettierignore](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/.prettierignore)\n- [.prettierrc.json](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/.prettierrc.json)\n- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)\n- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)\n- [LICENSE](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/LICENSE)\n- [README.md](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/README.md)\n- [index.d.ts](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/index.d.ts)\n- [index.js](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/index.js)\n- [index.spec.mjs](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/index.spec.mjs)\n- [package-lock.json](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/package-lock.json)\n- [package.json](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/package.json)\n- [tsconfig.json](https://github.com/osm-americana/diplomat/blob/main/tsconfig.json)\n\n## README\n\n# Diplomat\n\nDiplomat prepares your interactive map for an international audience. With a few lines of code, your [MapLibre GL JS](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js/)–powered map will speak the user’s preferred language while informing them about local languages the world over.\n\nBefore\nAfter\n\n## Features\n\nDiplomat gives all parties a win-win:\n\n- Tailors labels to the user’s preferred language.\n\n- Respects multilingualism with optional dual language labels: both the user’s preferred language and the local native language.\n\n- Recognizes any language, dialect, or script out of the box with sophisticated language code matching.\n\nDiplomat lets your designer save face:\n\n- Uses space efficiently with both multiline and inline label layouts.\n\n- Deduplicates names within a label to avoid clutter.\n\n- Preserves diacritics in English exonyms where appropriate.\n\n- Respects right-to-left and vertical text layouts.\n\nDiplomat works quietly behind the scenes:\n\n- Changes the style on the fly at runtime – no need to publish a new style or tileset for every language.\n\n- You choose which style layers to localize, or localize them all automatically.\n\n- Supports multiple popular vector tile schemas without hacky workarounds, plus custom vector tilesets and GeoJSON sources.\n\nAll localization is subject to the availability of localized names in the map data source. See [the caveats](#caveats) for more details.\n\n## Requirements\n\nDiplomat is compatible with applications using MapLibre GL JS v5.13.0 and above.\n\nThe stylesheet must use the newer [expression](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/expressions/) syntax; [legacy style functions](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/deprecations/#function) are not supported. The stylesheet’s sources must conform to [Diplomat’s schema](#schema). Several popular vector tilesets already conform to this schema, including:\n\n- [OpenMapTiles](https://openmaptiles.org/schema/) implementations, e.g., [MapTiler](https://cloud.maptiler.com/tiles/v3-openmaptiles/), [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org/), [OpenStreetMap U.S.](https://tiles.openstreetmap.us/vector/openmaptiles/), [Stadia Maps](https://docs.stadiamaps.com/vector/)\n\n- [Tilezen](https://tilezen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/layers/) implementations, e.g., [Protomaps](https://protomaps.com/)\n\nWith additional configuration, Diplomat supports even more vector tilesets, including:\n\n- [Mapbox Streets](https://docs.mapbox.com/data/tilesets/reference/mapbox-streets-v8/#names)\n\n- [OpenHistoricalMap](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/OpenHistoricalMap/Reuse#Vector_tiles)\n\n- [Shortbread](https://shortbread-tiles.org/schema/) implementations, e.g., [OpenStreetMap.org](https://vector.openstreetmap.org/), [VersaTiles](https://github.com/versatiles-org/versatiles-generator/)\n\n## Installation\n\nThis plugin is available as [an NPM package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@americana/diplomat). To install it, run the following command:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnpm install @americana/diplomat\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAlternatively, you can include the plugin as a standalone script from a CDN such as [unpkg](https://unpkg.com/@americana/diplomat/index.js).\n\n## Usage\n\nImport Diplomat as a module:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport * as Diplomat from \"@americana/diplomat\";\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAfter creating an instance of &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96;, register an event listener for the &#96;styledata&#96; event that localizes the map:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.once(\"styledata\", (event) =&gt; {\nDiplomat.localizeStyle(map);\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf your stylesheet uses a tileset that formats the name keys differently, such as OpenHistoricalMap or Shortbread, set the format when localizing the layers, for example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.once(\"styledata\", (event) =&gt; {\nlet locales = Diplomat.getLocales();\nDiplomat.localizeStyle(map, locales, {\nlocalizedNamePropertyFormat: \"name_$1\",\n});\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf you set the &#96;hash&#96; option to a string when creating the &#96;Map&#96;, you can have this code respond to a &#96;language&#96; parameter in the URL hash. Add a window event listener for whenever the hash changes, in order to update the layers:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\naddEventListener(\"hashchange\", (event) =&gt; {\nlet oldLanguage = Diplomat.getLanguageFromURL(new URL(event.oldURL));\nlet newLanguage = Diplomat.getLanguageFromURL(new URL(event.newURL));\n\nif (oldLanguage !== newLanguage) {\nDiplomat.localizeStyle(map);\n}\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSimilarly, you can immediately respond to any change the user makes to their browser language preference in real time:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\naddEventListener(\"languagechange\", (event) =&gt; {\nDiplomat.localizeStyle(map);\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote\n\nBy default, MapLibre GL JS does not support bidirectional text. Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages will be unreadable unless you [install the mapbox-gl-rtl-text plugin](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/examples/add-support-for-right-to-left-scripts/).\n\n## Schema\n\nDiplomat can manipulate any GeoJSON or vector tile source, as long as it includes the following properties on each feature:\n\n- &#96;name&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): The name in the local or official language. You can customize this property by setting the &#96;unlocalizedNameProperty&#96; option when calling [&#96;maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibreglmapprototypelocalizestyle).\n\n- &#96;name:xyz&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): The name in another language, where xyz is a valid [IETF language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag). For example, &#96;name:zh&#96; for Chinese, &#96;name:zh-Hant&#96; for Traditional Chinese, &#96;name:zh-Hant-TW&#96; for Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), and &#96;name:zh-Latn-pinyin&#96; for Chinese in pinyin. You can customize this format by setting the &#96;localizedNamePropertyFormat&#96; option when calling [&#96;maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibreglmapprototypelocalizestyle).\n\nFor compatibility with the [OpenMapTiles](https://openmaptiles.org/schema/) schema, &#96;name_en&#96; and &#96;name_de&#96; are also recognized as alternatives to &#96;name:en&#96; and &#96;name:de&#96; for English and German, respectively, but only in the &#96;transportation_name&#96; layer. For performance reasons, Diplomat does not look for this format by default for any other language or layer.\n\nEach of the supported properties may be set to a list of values separated by [semicolons](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Semi-colon_value_separator). For example, if a place speaks both English and French, &#96;name&#96; should be &#96;English Name;French Name&#96;. Similarly, if a landmark has three equally common names in Spanish, regardless of dialect, &#96;name:es&#96; should be &#96;Nombre Uno;Nombre Dos;Nombre Tres&#96;. In the rare case that a single name contains a semicolon, it should be escaped as a double semicolon (&#96;;;&#96;).\n\n## API\n\nThis plugin adds several symbols to a &#96;maplibregl.Diplomat&#96; namespace and adds a single method to each instance of &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96;. The following documentation uses the notation &#96;maplibregl.Diplomat.*&#96; in case you include Diplomat as a script. However, if you import Diplomat as a module, these symbols are directly imported into your code, without any namespacing.\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.localizedName\n\nAn expression that produces the names in the user's preferred language, each on a separate line.\n\nUse this constant if you are building the entire stylesheet programmatically before initializing a &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96; and want more fine-grained control over which layers have which label layout than [&#96;maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibreglmapprototypelocalizestyle) provides.\n\nThis expression is appropriate for labeling a type of feature that almost always has a familiar translation in the user’s preferred language, such as the name of a country. It is also appropriate for minor features like points of interest, for which an extra local-language gloss would clutter the map.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.setLayoutProperty(\n\"country-labels\",\n\"text-field\",\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.localizedName,\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.localizedNameInline\n\nAn expression that produces the names in the user's preferred language, all on the same line.\n\nUse this constant if you are building the entire stylesheet programmatically before initializing a &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96; and want more fine-grained control over which layers have which label layout than [&#96;maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibreglmapprototypelocalizestyle) provides.\n\nThis expression is appropriate for labeling a linear feature, such as a road or waterway. The symbol layer’s [&#96;symbol-placement&#96;](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/layers/#symbol-placement) layout property should be set to either &#96;line&#96; or &#96;line-center&#96;.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.setLayoutProperty(\n\"road-labels\",\n\"text-field\",\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.localizedNameInline,\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibre.Diplomat.localizedNameWithLocalGloss\n\nAn expression that produces the name in the user's preferred language, followed by the name in the local language in parentheses if it differs.\n\nUse this constant if you are building the entire stylesheet programmatically before initializing a &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96; and want more fine-grained control over which layers have which label layout than [&#96;maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibreglmapprototypelocalizestyle) provides.\n\nThis expression is appropriate for labeling a type of feature that is only sometimes translated into user’s preferred language, such as the name of a city or town. The extra local-language gloss respects local customs and keeps the user informed, but it can also risk [information overload](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_overload) and crowd out other useful labels.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.setLayoutProperty(\n\"city-labels\",\n\"text-field\",\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.localizedNameWithGloss,\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.getLocalizedCountryNameExpression()\n\nReturns an expression that converts the given country code to a human-readable name in the user's preferred language.\n\nThis method is useful for stylesheets powered by OpenMapTiles, which only provides the ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the country on either side of a boundary, but not the full country name in any language.\n\nParameters:\n\n- &#96;code&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): An expression that evaluates to an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.setLayoutProperty(\n\"boundary-edge-labels\",\n\"text-field\",\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.getLocalizedCountryNameExpression([\"get\", \"adm0_l\"]),\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote\n\nUse [&#96;maplibregl.Diplomat.getGlobalStateForLocalization()&#96;](#maplibregldiplomatgetglobalstateforlocalization) to populate the global state required by this expression, then call [&#96;maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibreglmapprototypelocalizestyle). Otherwise, this expression evaluates to the raw country code.\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.getGlobalStateForLocalization()\n\nReturns the global state that Diplomat needs to fully localize the style.\n\nIf you are building a stylesheet programmatically, you can use this method to populate a &#96;state&#96; property at the root of the stylesheet before initializing a &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96;. You can add additional global state properties besides the ones that come from this object, as long as you avoid making a deep clone of the object.\n\nIf your stylesheet is powered by OpenMapTiles, you need to set this global state object in order to localizing boundary edge labels that come from the [&#96;boundary&#96;](https://openmaptiles.org/schema/#boundary) layer. Otherwise, the user will see only ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, because OpenMapTiles only provides these codes instead of the full country name on either side of a boundary.\n\nParameters:\n\n- &#96;locales&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): The locales for formatting the country names.\n\n- &#96;options.uppercaseCountryNames&#96; (&#96;boolean&#96;): Whether to write the country names in all uppercase, respecting the locale’s case conventions. Enable this option if you intend to display the boundary edge labels in uppercase, because the &#96;upcase&#96; expression operator is locale-insensitive.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.once(\"styledata\", (event) =&gt; {\nlet localizationState = maplibregl.Diplomat.getGlobalStateForLocalization(\ngetLocales(),\n{\nuppercaseCountryNames: true,\n},\n);\nfor (let [key, value] of Object.entries(localizationState)) {\nmap.setGlobalStateProperty(key, value);\n}\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.getLocales()\n\nReturns the languages that the user prefers.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.getLocales().includes(\"en\");\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.getRelatedLanguageTags()\n\nReturns an array of the language tags related to the given language tag, sorted from most specific to least specific.\n\nParameters:\n\n- &#96;tag&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): The language tag that the returned language tags are related to.\n\nReturns a sorted array of related language tags, or an empty array if &#96;tag&#96; is malformed.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.getRelatedLanguageTags(\"sr-RS\").includes(\"sr-Cyrl\");\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.getRelatedLanguageTags(\"zh\").includes(\"zh-Hans-CN\");\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibregl.Diplomat.localizeStyle()\n\nUpdates each style layer's &#96;text-field&#96; value to match the given locales, upgrading any unlocalizable layer along the way.\n\nIf neither &#96;options.layers&#96; nor &#96;options.sourceLayers&#96; is specified in &#96;options&#96;, this function makes localizable any style layer that gets the feature property specified in &#96;options.unlocalizedNameProperty&#96;, or &#96;name&#96; by default.\n\nParameters:\n\n- &#96;map&#96; (&#96;maplibregl.Map&#96;): The map to localize.\n\n- &#96;locales&#96; (&#96;[string]&#96;): The locales to insert into each layer, as a comma-separated list of [IETF language tags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag). Uses the &#96;language&#96; URL hash parameter or browser preferences by default.\n\n- &#96;options&#96; (&#96;object&#96;):\n\n&#96;layers&#96; (&#96;[string]&#96;): The style layers with these IDs will be made localizable.\n&#96;sourceLayers&#96; (&#96;[string]&#96;): The style layers that use these source layers will be made localizable. These are source layer IDs, not style layer IDs.\n&#96;unlocalizedNameProperty&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): The name of the property holding the unlocalized name. &#96;name&#96; by default.\n&#96;localizedNamePropertyFormat&#96; (&#96;string&#96;): The format of properties holding localized names, where &#96;$1&#96; is replaced by an IETF language tag. &#96;name:$1&#96; by default.\n&#96;glossLocalNames&#96; (&#96;boolean&#96;): Whether to format each label as a dual language label including a local name gloss.\n&#96;uppercaseCountryNames&#96; (&#96;boolean&#96;): Whether to write country names in all uppercase, respecting the locale’s case conventions.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmaplibregl.Diplomat.localizeStyle(map, [\"eo\"], {\nsourceLayers: [\"place\"],\nglossLocalNames: true,\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### maplibregl.Map.prototype.localizeStyle()\n\nA wrapper for [&#96;maplibregl.Diplomat.localizeStyle()&#96;](#maplibregldiplomatlocalizestyle) that does not require passing in a &#96;maplibregl.Map&#96;. Only available when including Diplomat as a script.\n\nExample:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nmap.localizeStyle([\"eo\"], {\nlocalizedNamePropertyFormat: \"name_$1\",\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Caveats\n\nDiplomat only switches between languages that are present in the stylesheet’s data sources. It does not fetch translations from other sources or generate its own transliterations. By convention, [OpenStreetMap’s coverage in some regions](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Multilingual_names) is largely limited to locally spoken languages. If you need more comprehensive coverage in a given language, consider using a tileset that combines names from OpenStreetMap and Wikidata, such as the [OpenStreetMap U.S. Tileservice](https://tiles.openstreetmap.us/vector/openmaptiles/).\n\nBy default, MapLibre GL JS does not support bidirectional text. Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages will be unreadable unless you [install the mapbox-gl-rtl-text plugin](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/examples/add-support-for-right-to-left-scripts/).\n\nDiplomat performs basic language fallbacks according to the [ICU locale fallback algorithm](https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/locale/#fallback). Additionally, it implements the [Likely Subtags](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/#Likely_Subtags) algorithm of Unicode Technical Standard #35, so for example requesting either &#96;zh&#96; or &#96;cmn&#96; returns a name tagged as &#96;zh-Hans-CN&#96;, among other variations. However, in general, it does not fall back to a related but distinct language code, such as from &#96;sr-Cyrl&#96; to &#96;ru&#96; or from &#96;nb&#96; to &#96;no&#96;. Instead, the user can [set their preferred languages](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-lang-priorities) in their browser or operating system settings.\n\nFor historical reasons, [OpenStreetMap’s coverage in many reasons](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Multilingual_names) encodes multiple local names separated by human-readable punctuation. Diplomat makes no attempt to guess which punctuation is part of a name and which punctuation delimits two names.\n\n## Acknowledgments\n\nThis plugin was spun out of the [OpenStreetMap Americana](https://github.com/osm-americana/openstreetmap-americana/) project. It was originally inspired by [Mapbox GL Language](https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gl-language/)."

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Implementing style switcher**

I'm implementing the map style switcher using MapGLStyleSwitcher component with proper map reference handling. I need to pass the map reference to MapGLStyleSwitcher so it can control the map style via the Map's `mapStyle` prop. I'm using react-map-gl's `useMap` hook to access the map instance in MapGLStyleSwitcher. I'm updating the style switcher to use `onAfterStyleChange` callback for setting the map style. 

**Updating style switcher**

I'm switching to use `mapStyle` prop instead of `styleUrl` for triggering map updates. MapLibre Transition plugin can enable smooth style transitions, contrary to my initial assumption. I discovered that maplibre-transition plugin handles feature-level transitions, not style transitions. I'll add the maplibre-transition plugin and test if it supports style transitions via the demo page. 

**Adding transition plugin**

I'm adding the maplibre-transition plugin and calling `MaplibreTransition.init(map)` in the map's `onLoad` callback. I'm adding Carto styles: positron, voyager, dark matter to the map. I'm implementing maplibre-transition for style transitions and will handle the diplomat rerun on style change. I'm adding maplibre-transition plugin for smooth style transitions and will initialize it with MaplibreTransition.init(map). I'm adding maplibre-transition plugin for smooth style transitions and initializing it with MaplibreTransition.init(map). I'm initializing MaplibreTransition.init(map) in the onLoad callback to ensure proper setup. 

I'm importing MaplibreTransition and Diplomat, and adding state for mapStyle and a ref for the map component. 

**Handling map instance**

I'm storing the map instance from react-map-gl's onLoad event in a ref instead of trying to access it through the component ref. 

**Adding style switching**

I'm adding map-gl-style-switcher and maplibre-transition for style transition support. I'm adding refs and state management for the style switcher component. 

**Handling style events**

I'm updating the style event handling to ensure styledata fires correctly on both initial load and style changes. I'll use map.on('styledata', ...) to handle both initial load and style changes consistently. 

I'll use map.on('styledata', ...) to handle style changes consistently, since map.once only runs once and we need to capture all style updates. I'm listening for styledata events to capture style changes when mapStyle prop updates. </details></think>

[Introduction \| react-map-gl](https://visgl.github.io/react-map-gl/docs)<br/><br/># @vis.gl/react-maplibre: onLoad and useMap<br/><br/>## onLoad Callback<br/><br/>The `Map` component from `@vis.gl/react-maplibre` supports an `onLoad` event handler that fires when the map finishes loading.[2] This allows you to execute code after the map is ready.<br/><br/>## useMap Hook<br/><br/>`@vis.gl/react-maplibre` provides React hooks and context interfaces to access the underlying map instance.[1] The `useMap` hook allows you to get a reference to the map object within child components, enabling you to interact with the map programmatically.<br/><br/>## Basic Usage<br/><br/>The library wraps MapLibre GL JS as a fully controlled reactive React component.[1][2] You can initialize it with `initialViewState` to set the starting view, and use props like `mapStyle`, `longitude`, `latitude`, and `zoom` to control the map's state reactively through React.<br/><br/>```tsx<br/>import \{ Map \} from '@vis.gl/react-maplibre';<br/><br/><Map<br/>  initialViewState=\{{ longitude: -122.4, latitude: 37.8, zoom: 14 \}}<br/>  mapStyle="https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json"<br/>  onLoad=\{/* callback */\}<br/>/><br/>```<br/><br/>The key design philosophy is that the map is a fully controlled component—all state flows through React props rather than the map managing its own internal state.[5] |

As you move the cursor across the map, the event will fire every time the cursor changes position within the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onMouseLeave: (event: MapLayerMouseEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a pointing device (usually a mouse) leaves a visible portion of the layer(s) specified by&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; or moves from the layer to outside the map canvas.\n\n#### onMouseOut: (event: MapLayerMouseEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a point device (usually a mouse) leaves the map's canvas.\n\n#### onClick: (event: MapLayerMouseEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a pointing device (usually a mouse) is pressed and released at the same point on the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onDblClick: (event: MapLayerMouseEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a pointing device (usually a mouse) is pressed and released twice at the same point on the map in rapid succession.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onContextMenu: (event: MapLayerMouseEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when the right button of the mouse is clicked or the context menu key is pressed within the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onWheel: (event: MapWheelEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a wheel event occurs within the map.\n\n#### onTouchStart: (event: MapLayerTouchEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a&#96;touchstart&#96; event occurs within the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onTouchEnd: (event: MapLayerTouchEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a&#96;touchend&#96; event occurs within the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onTouchMove: (event: MapLayerTouchEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a&#96;touchmove&#96; event occurs within the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onTouchCancel: (event: MapLayerTouchEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a&#96;touchcancel&#96; event occurs within the map.\n\nIf&#96;interactiveLayerIds&#96; is specified, the event will contain an additional&#96;features&#96; field that contains features under the cursor from the specified layer.\n\n#### onMoveStart: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just before the map begins a transition from one view to another.\n\n#### onMove: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled repeatedly during an animated transition from one view to another.\n\nWhen&#96;Map&#96; is used as a controlled component,&#96;event.viewState&#96; reflects the view state that the camera \"proposes\" to move to, as a result of either user interaction or methods such as [flyTo](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/classes/Map/#flyto). The camera does not actually change until the application updates the view state props (&#96;longitude&#96;,&#96;latitude&#96;,&#96;zoom&#96; etc.). See [state management](https://visgl.github.io/react-maplibre/docs/get-started/state-management) for examples.\n\n#### onMoveEnd: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just after the map completes a transition from one view to another.\n\n#### onDragStart: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a \"drag to pan\" interaction starts.\n\n#### onDrag: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled repeatedly during a \"drag to pan\" interaction.\n\n#### onDragEnd: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a \"drag to pan\" interaction ends.\n\n#### onZoomStart: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just before the map begins a transition from one zoom level to another.\n\n#### onZoom: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled repeatedly during an animated transition from one zoom level to another.\n\nWhen&#96;Map&#96; is used as a controlled component,&#96;event.viewState.zoom&#96; reflects the zoom that the camera \"proposes\" to change to, as a result of either user interaction or methods such as [flyTo](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/classes/Map/#flyto). The camera does not actually change until the application updates the&#96;zoom&#96; prop.\n\n#### onZoomEnd: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just after the map completes a transition from one zoom level to another.\n\n#### onRotateStart: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just before the map begins a transition from one bearing (rotation) to another.\n\n#### onRotate: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled repeatedly during an animated transition from one bearing (rotation) to another.\n\nWhen&#96;Map&#96; is used as a controlled component,&#96;event.viewState.bearing&#96; reflects the zoom that the camera \"proposes\" to change to, as a result of either user interaction or methods such as [flyTo](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/classes/Map/#flyto). The camera does not actually change until the application updates the&#96;bearing&#96; prop.\n\n#### onRotateEnd: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just after the map completes a transition from one bearing (rotation) to another.\n\n#### onPitchStart: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just before the map begins a transition from one pitch (tilt) to another.\n\n#### onPitch: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled repeatedly during an animated transition from one pitch (tilt) to another.\n\nWhen&#96;Map&#96; is used as a controlled component,&#96;event.viewState.pitch&#96; reflects the zoom that the camera \"proposes\" to change to, as a result of either user interaction or methods such as [flyTo](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/classes/Map/#flyto). The camera does not actually change until the application updates the&#96;pitch&#96; prop.\n\n#### onPitchEnd: (event: ViewStateChangeEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled just after the map completes a transition from one pitch (tilt) to another.\n\n#### onBoxZoomStart: (event: MapBoxZoomEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a \"box zoom\" interaction starts.\n\n#### onBoxZoomEnd: (event: MapBoxZoomEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when a \"box zoom\" interaction ends.\n\n#### onBoxZoomCancel: (event:MapBoxZoomEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when the user cancels a \"box zoom\" interaction, or when the bounding box does not meet the minimum size threshold.\n\n#### onData: (event: MapStyleDataEvent | MapSourceDataEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when any map data loads or changes. See [MapDataEvent](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/type-aliases/MapDataEvent/) for more information.\n\n#### onStyleData: (event: MapStyleDataEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when the map's style loads or changes. See [MapDataEvent](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/type-aliases/MapDataEvent/) for more information.\n\n#### onSourceData: (event: MapSourceDataEvent) =&gt; void​\n\nCalled when one of the map's sources loads or changes, including if a tile belonging to a source loads or changes. See [MapDataEvent](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/type-aliases/MapDataEvent/) for more information.\n\n### Other options​\n\nThe following props, along with any [options](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/type-aliases/MapOptions/) of the&#96;Map&#96; class not listed above, can be specified to construct the underlying&#96;Map&#96; instance.\n\nNote: props in this section are not reactive. They are only used once when the Map instance is constructed.\n\n#### mapLib: any​\n\nDefault:\n\n- &#96;import('maplibre-gl')&#96;\n\nSpecify the underlying base map library for the Map component. The value can be provided with several options:\n\nBy module import (and embedding in the final bundle):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport * as React from 'react';import {Map} from '@vis.gl/react-maplibre';import maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';function App() {  return &lt;Map mapLib={maplibregl} /&gt;;}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy dynamic import (thus enable bundle splitting):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport * as React from 'react';import {Map} from '@vis.gl/react-maplibre';function App() {  return &lt;Map mapLib={import('maplibre-gl')} /&gt;;}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOr to load a pre-bundled version of the library:\n\nindex.html\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;script src=\"https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.js\" &gt;&lt;/script&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\napp.tsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport * as React from 'react';import {Map} from '@vis.gl/react-maplibre';function App() {  return &lt;Map mapLib={window.maplibregl} /&gt;;}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### maxParallelImageRequests: number​\n\nDefault:&#96;16&#96;\n\nThe maximum number of images (raster tiles, sprites, icons) to load in parallel.\n\n#### reuseMaps: boolean​\n\nDefault:&#96;false&#96;\n\nBy default, every time a map component is unmounted, all internal resources associated with the underlying&#96;Map&#96; instance are released. If the map gets mounted again, a new&#96;Map&#96; instance is constructed.\n\nIf&#96;reuseMaps&#96; is set to&#96;true&#96;, when a map component is unmounted, the underlying&#96;Map&#96; instance is retained in memory. The next time a map component gets mounted, the saved instance is reused. This behavior may be desirable if an application frequently mounts/unmounts map(s), for example in a tabbed or collapsable UI, and wants to avoid recreating the Map and its data cache triggered by initialization.\n\nNote that since some map options cannot be modified after initialization, when reusing maps, only the reactive props and&#96;initialViewState&#96; of the new  instantiated on a page with maplibre-gl maps.\n\n#### workerUrl: string​\n\nProvides an interface for loading maplibre-gl's WebWorker bundle from a self-hosted URL. This is useful if your site needs to operate in a strict CSP (Content Security Policy) environment wherein you are not allowed to load JavaScript code from a Blob URL, which iare safe to call without breaking the React bindings. Integración aplicada. Resumen de cambios:

## Cambios realizados

### 1. **map-gl-style-switcher**
- Selector de estilos en la esquina inferior izquierda del mapa.
- Tres estilos Carto: **Positron** (claro), **Voyager** (calles) y **Dark Matter** (oscuro).
- Tema `auto` según preferencia del sistema.
- Al cambiar de estilo se actualiza el mapa.

### 2. **Diplomat** (@americana/diplomat)
- Localiza etiquetas del mapa al idioma del navegador.
- Se ejecuta al cargar el mapa y cada vez que cambia el estilo.
- Usa el esquema de nombres de OpenMapTiles (compatible con Carto).

### 3. **maplibre-transition**
- Inicializado en el mapa.
- Pensado para transiciones de propiedades de features (ej. `fill-opacity`).
- El plugin de MapLibre para transiciones entre estilos no está disponible en este paquete; el cambio de estilo se hace de forma instantánea.

---

## Cómo probar

Ejecuta el servidor de desarrollo:

```bash
pnpm dev
```

El mapa debería mostrar:
- Un selector de estilos en la esquina inferior izquierda.
- Etiquetas en el idioma del navegador.
- Tres estilos disponibles: Positron, Voyager y Dark Matter.

Nota: el fallo de build (`@vercel/turbopack-next/internal/font/google/font`) parece ser un problema de Next.js/Turbopack con fuentes, no relacionado con estos cambios.

[Map inspect tool – OpenMapTiles](https://openmaptiles.org/inspect/)<br/><br/># OpenMapTiles Vector Tile Schema and Carto Basemaps<br/><br/>The OpenMapTiles project provides an open vector tile schema designed for OpenStreetMap layers.[1][2] The schema was initially modeled after the cartography of the **Carto Basemap Positron**.[2]<br/><br/>## Schema Overview<br/><br/>The OpenMapTiles schema is open-source (CC-BY licensed) and organizes vector data into multiple thematic layers.[2] Key layers include aerodrome_label, aeroway, boundary, building, landcover, landuse, place, poi, transportation, water, and waterway, among others.[2]<br/><br/>Each layer contains specific **property fields** (attributes). For example, the aerodrome_label layer includes properties like `name`, `name_en`, `name_de`, `class`, `iata`, `icao`, `ele`, and `ele_ft`.[2]<br/><br/>## Available Basemap Styles<br/><br/>OpenMapTiles comes with several pre-built map styles optimized for the schema:[1]<br/>- OSM OpenMapTiles (based on OpenStreetMap Carto)<br/>- MapTiler Basic<br/>- OSM Bright<br/>- Positron<br/>- Dark Matter<br/>- Fiord Color<br/>- Toner<br/><br/>All styles and schema are free and open-source, allowing you to use them as basemaps or starting points for custom map designs.[1] The schema has been refined through cooperation with the Wikimedia Foundation and incorporates extensive experience in creating maps from OpenStreetMap data.[2] |

[OpenStreetMap in English – OpenMapTiles](https://openmaptiles.org/languages/en/)<br/><br/># Diplomat: Multilingual Map Localization for OpenMapTiles<br/><br/>**Diplomat** is a JavaScript internationalization plugin for MapLibre GL JS that enables multilingual map support.[1] It works with map styles using the newer expression syntax and is compatible with MapLibre GL JS v5.13.0 and above.[1]<br/><br/>## Key Features<br/><br/>Diplomat automatically tailors map labels to users' preferred languages while offering optional dual-language labels showing both the user's language and local names.[1] It efficiently handles multilingual display through multiline and inline label layouts, deduplicates names to reduce clutter, and respects right-to-left and vertical text orientations.[1]<br/><br/>## OpenMapTiles Compatibility<br/><br/>Diplomat seamlessly integrates with OpenMapTiles implementations.[1] OpenMapTiles are inherently multilingual, supporting display in numerous languages including English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, Arabic, Japanese, and many others.[3] The plugin works with popular vector tile services that follow the OpenMapTiles schema, such as MapTiler, OpenFreeMap, and Stadia Maps.[1]<br/><br/>## Technical Implementation<br/><br/>The plugin uses MapLibre GL's expression syntax—represented as JSON arrays with operators and arguments—to dynamically modify map styles at runtime without requiring republication.[1][2] This allows language switching without changing the underlying tileset or style files.[1]<br/><br/>Diplomat is available as an NPM package (@americana/diplomat) and is open-source under the CC0-1.0 license.[1] |

He aplicado estos cambios para que la localización funcione:

## Cambios realizados

### 1. **Estilos Carto → OpenFreeMap**
Los estilos Carto usan tokens legacy (`{name_en}`) que Diplomat no puede modificar. Se han sustituido por estilos de **OpenFreeMap**, que usan OpenMapTiles con expresiones y son compatibles con Diplomat.

Estilos disponibles ahora:
- **Liberty** (por defecto)
- **Positron**
- **Bright**
- **Dark**

### 2. **Configuración de Diplomat para OpenMapTiles**
OpenMapTiles usa propiedades como `name_es`, `name_en`, etc. Se ha añadido la opción:

```ts
localizedNamePropertyFormat: 'name_$1'
```

### 3. **Atribución**
Se ha reactivado la atribución del mapa, como exige OpenFreeMap.

---

## Cómo comprobar la localización

1. Cambia el idioma del navegador (por ejemplo, a español).
2. Recarga la página.
3. Las etiquetas del mapa deberían mostrarse en ese idioma cuando existan traducciones en los datos de OpenStreetMap.

**Nota:** La cobertura depende de los datos de OSM. En España suele haber buenas traducciones para `name_es`.
